title: Convoy UGS-72 at the Strait of Gibraltar, 17 February 1945
eyebrow: The Atlantic · USS Solar (DE-221) in the escort of UGS-72, Hampton Roads to the Mediterranean

participants.name: U-300
participants.note: Credited with the attack by the postwar accounts (uboat.net, after Rohwer). The German records read put her orders in the Gibraltar area from 6 February; the Naval Staff credited the attack to U 869 on the day. No record of hers for the attack is entered.

paras.text: Two ships of convoy UGS-72, the Liberty ship Michael J. Stone and the British tanker Regent Lion, were torpedoed as the convoy entered the Strait of Gibraltar on the morning of 17 February 1945. USS Solar, one of the escorts, logged both as "struck by torpedo or mine" and took Michael J. Stone into Gibraltar Bay.

Solar's war diary for February 1945 records Regent Lion "struck by torpedo or mine, settling by the stern but not sinking" at 1055, and Michael J. Stone the same at 1105, at 35°-57'N 5°-50'W, the convoy in four columns ([[cite:rg38-139905513/p03|war diary, p. 3]]). At 1121 Solar was sent to search under the escort division's commander; at 1304 she was ordered to relieve USS Kearny (DD-432) and escort Michael J. Stone to Gibraltar, where she arrived at 1545, leaving again at 1700 to overtake the convoy's Southern France section.

The Navy's summary of Michael J. Stone's survivors' statements, of 26 March 1945, has her "torpedoed at 0955 GMT, 17 Feb 45, in 35.55N - 05.51W", struck on the starboard side between holds 4 and 5, third ship in the fourth column of about 86; the torpedo's track was not seen, "The sub was not sighted", and all 73 aboard survived ([[cite:marad:MichaelJStone_3359_002|Op-16-B-5]]).

The German Naval Staff's war diary for the day credits the sinking, from a radio-intelligence report, "probably" to U 869 ([[cite:skl66/p183|vol. 66, p. 183]]). U-869's wreck lies off New Jersey, so that credit cannot stand. On 6 February the U-boat command's situation report has U-300 (Hein) asking for, and given, the Gibraltar operations area ([[cite:bdu-feb45/760|B.d.U. report 760]]), and the postwar accounts credit U-300 with the attack: two spreads of two torpedoes, 27 miles from Gibraltar. U-300 was depth-charged by HMS Evadne and scuttled under the gunfire of HMS Recruit and HMS Pincher west of Cádiz on 22 February 1945, with nine dead, among them her commander, and 41 taken prisoner. No record of U-300's own for 17 February is entered here, and the Naval Staff's diary for the month does not name her.

The survivors' summary is headed "ALL TIMES GMT": 0955. The Naval Staff's 1100 is German time, an hour ahead of GMT (zone A, −1), so 1000 GMT, assumed. Solar's diary types no zone, and her track takes zone Z from her longitude (assumed): her 1105 for Michael J. Stone is then seventy minutes after the survivors' time. In zone A it would be 1005 GMT, ten minutes after it, which points to her clock being an hour ahead of GMT entering the Strait; no record says so, and her track keeps zone Z until one does.

- The British interrogation report on U-300's 41 survivors (the Admiralty's C.B. 04051 series; the UK National Archives, ADM 186 or ADM 199): the boat's own account of the attack. - The U-boat command's war diary for 17-22 February 1945. - Michael J. Stone's Armed Guard report (NARA, RG 38) and Regent Lion's master's report. - Kearny's and the escort commander's war diaries for 17 February, which may give the convoy's own clock and the search. - A recognition silhouette of U-300's type, traced from a plate.

events.placed: The day of the report; no time
events.words: "U-300 (Hein) reports position from BF 17, requests operations area Gibraltar." (The request is granted, the report says, because the boat had already gone far outbound.)
Entering Straits of Gibraltar. Convoy in four columns.
events.note: The diary types no zone; zone Z is taken from her longitude, as her track takes it (assumed).

events.words: "The MICHAEL J. STONE was torpedoed at 0955 GMT, 17 Feb 45, in 35.55N - 05.51W ... At 0955 a torpedo struck on the starboard side abreast of bulkhead between #4 and #5 holds ... Track of torpedo was not seen ... all 73 survived. ... The sub was not sighted."
events.source: Op-16-B-5, summary of statements by survivors of the SS Michael J. Stone, 26 Mar 1945 ("ALL TIMES GMT")

events.words: (The postwar account) Two spreads of two torpedoes fired at convoy UGS-72, 27 miles from Gibraltar; Michael J. Stone hit in station 43, and Regent Lion.
events.source: uboat.net, ships hit by U-300 (after Rohwer)
events.note: The account's time; German boats kept German time, taken as zone A (−1) (assumed).

events.original: Nach B-Meldung wurde um 1100 Uhr vor Gibraltar ein Schiff torpediert; wahrscheinlich Erfolg von U 869.
events.translation: According to a radio-intelligence (B-Dienst) report, a ship was torpedoed off Gibraltar at 1100; probably a success by U 869.
events.source: German Naval Staff war diary, Teil A, vol. 66, 17 Feb 1945, p. 183
events.note: The diary's 1100 carries no zone; German time (MEZ) is taken as zone A (−1) (assumed). The only entry on the attack in the month's volume; U 300 is not named in it.

events.words: SS Regent Lion in column one struck by torpedo or mine, settling by the stern but not sinking.
SS Michael J. Stone in column one struck by torpedo or mine, settling by the stern but not sinking.
Ordered to leave station on port side of convoy to conduct search under direction of CCD30 in USS KNOXVILLE (PF-64).
Ordered by CTG 60.9 to relieve USS KEARNY (DD-432) and escort SS Michael J. Stone to Gibraltar.
Arrived Gibraltar Bay. 1700 departed Gibraltar Bay to overtake USS KEARNY escorting Southern France section of UGS 72.

events.placed: The day; no time in the account
events.words: (The postwar account) After depth-charge damage from HMS Evadne, U-300 is scuttled under the gunfire of HMS Recruit and HMS Pincher west of Cádiz; nine dead, among them her commander, and 41 survivors.
events.source: uboat.net, U-300 and Fritz Hein (after Niestlé and Busch and Röll)

claims.answer: U-300 was given the Gibraltar operations area on 6 February
claims.note: Puts the boat's orders in the area eleven days before, not the boat at the attack

claims.question: Which U-boat?
claims.source: German Naval Staff war diary, vol. 66, 17 Feb 1945, p. 183
claims.note: The Naval Staff's credit on the day, from a radio-intelligence report of the sinking, not from a boat's report. U-869 had been ordered to the Gibraltar area; her wreck lies off New Jersey (below)

claims.question: Which U-boat?
claims.answer: Not U-869, whose wreck was found off New Jersey
claims.note: The wreck found by divers in 1991 and identified as U-869; she cannot have been off Gibraltar on 17 February

claims.question: When were the ships hit, by one clock?
claims.note: The memorandum is headed "ALL TIMES GMT"

claims.question: When were the ships hit, by one clock?
claims.answer: Solar's diary was an hour ahead of GMT (zone A)
claims.note: Her 1105 for Michael J. Stone is 1005 GMT in zone A, ten minutes from the survivors' 0955 GMT, and seventy in zone Z, which her track assumes; the Naval Staff's 1100, German time, is 1000 GMT. Nothing in the diary names its zone, so her track keeps Z until a record does

claims.question: What became of Regent Lion?
claims.answer: Grounded on Perl Rock, a mile south of Carnero Point, and declared a total loss
claims.note: Taken in tow by HMS Rollicker and HMS Arctic Ranger on 19 February, by this account

claims.question: What became of Regent Lion?
claims.answer: Towed to Tangier and written off
claims.source: German Wikipedia, U 300 (after Busch and Röll, and Blair)
claims.note: Disagrees with the account above on where she ended
